section.heading: Corporations Act restructuring practitioner cannot be appointed if special administrator appointed

content.p: A restructuring practitioner for an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander corporation cannot be appointed under Part 5.3B of the Corporations Act (as applied by section 522-1 of this Act) if:
the corporation is under special administration under Part 11-2; or
the Registrar:
has given the corporation a notice under subsection 487-10(1); and
has not given the corporation a notice under subsection 487-10(5).

Paragraph (1)(b) does not apply if the Registrar has consented in writing to the appointment of the restructuring practitioner under Part 5.3B of the Corporations Act (as applied by section 522-1 of this Act).
A consent under subsection (2) to the appointment of a restructuring practitioner is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Effect of appointment of special administrator—Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander corporation under restructuring

content.p: If:
a restructuring practitioner for an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander corporation is appointed under Part 5.3B of the Corporations Act (as applied by section 522-1 of this Act); and
while that appointment continues, a special administrator for the corporation is appointed under Part 11-2; and
at the time the special administrator is appointed, the corporation has not made a restructuring plan;
the restructuring of the corporation under Part 5.3B of the Corporations Act (as applied by section 522-1 of this Act) ends on the day on which the special administrator is appointed.

section.heading: Effect of appointment of special administrator—Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander corporation subject to restructuring plan

content.p: This section applies if:
an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander corporation makes a restructuring plan under Part 5.3B of the Corporations Act (as applied by section 522-1 of this Act); and
before the plan terminates, a special administrator for the corporation is appointed under Part 11-2.
The Court may order that the restructuring plan is to terminate.
The order may be made on the application of:
the Registrar; or
the special administrator for the corporation; or
any other interested person.
The order may be made subject to conditions.
Effect of termination of restructuring plan

If the Court orders that the restructuring plan is to terminate, any admissible debt or claim that has not been dealt with in accordance with the restructuring plan is taken to be due and payable on the business day after the day on which the termination occurs.
In this section:
admissible debt or claim has the same meaning as in the Corporations Regulations 2001.

(2) The Commissioner may recover all or part of the excess from a person (the debtor) described in subsection (3) as a debt due by the debtor to the Commonwealth if the conditions specified in subsection (4) are met.
The persons from whom the Commissioner may recover are as follows:
the superannuation provider for the fund to which the payment was made;
if the payment, or an amount wholly or partly attributable to that payment, was transferred to another fund—the superannuation provider for that other fund.
The conditions for recovery are that:
the Commissioner gave the debtor written notice, as prescribed by the regulations, of the proposed recovery and the amount to be recovered; and
at least 28 days have passed since the notice was given; and
the amount recovered is not more than the amount specified in the notice.

Despite subsections (2) and (3), if the Commissioner gives a notice described in paragraph (4)(a) to a superannuation provider for a fund, and the fund does not hold an amount attributable to the payment, the Commissioner cannot recover from the superannuation provider.
The Commissioner may revoke a notice described in paragraph (4)(a).
The total of the amounts recovered from different debtors in relation to the same excess must not be more than the excess.
A notice described in paragraph (4)(a) is not a legislative instrument.
